title: Top-rated movies (100k+ votes)
description: The classic: best-rated movies that lots of people have voted on.
sql:
-- Top-rated movies
SELECT t.primary_title, t.premiered AS year, r.rating, r.votes
FROM ratings r JOIN titles t ON t.title_id = r.title_id
WHERE r.votes > 100000 AND +t.type = 'movie'  -- the "+" keeps SQLite from using the type index (faster)
ORDER BY r.rating DESC, r.votes DESC
LIMIT 50

title: Top-rated TV shows (100k+ votes)
description: Series and miniseries with more than 100,000 votes, best rated first.
sql:
SELECT t.primary_title, t.premiered AS start_year, t.ended AS end_year,
       r.rating, r.votes
FROM ratings r JOIN titles t ON t.title_id = r.title_id
WHERE r.votes > 100000 AND +t.type IN ('tvSeries', 'tvMiniSeries')  -- the "+" keeps SQLite from using the type index (faster)
ORDER BY r.rating DESC, r.votes DESC
LIMIT 50

title: Actors in the most movies with 100k+ votes
description: Actors/actresses ranked by how many movies with more than 100,000 votes they appear in, with the average rating of those movies.
sql:
WITH big AS (
  SELECT r.title_id, r.rating
  FROM ratings r JOIN titles t ON t.title_id = r.title_id
  WHERE r.votes > 100000 AND +t.type = 'movie'  -- the "+" keeps SQLite from using the type index (faster)
)
SELECT p.name, COUNT(*) AS big_movies, ROUND(AVG(big.rating), 2) AS avg_rating
FROM big
CROSS JOIN crew c ON c.title_id = big.title_id
JOIN people p ON p.person_id = c.person_id
WHERE c.category IN ('actor', 'actress')
GROUP BY c.person_id
ORDER BY big_movies DESC, avg_rating DESC
LIMIT 50

title: Actors by average rating of their big movies
description: Actors/actresses ranked by the average rating of their movies with 100k+ votes (at least 5 such movies). Takes a few seconds.
sql:
WITH big AS (
  SELECT r.title_id, r.rating, r.votes
  FROM ratings r JOIN titles t ON t.title_id = r.title_id
  WHERE r.votes > 100000 AND +t.type = 'movie'  -- the "+" keeps SQLite from using the type index (faster)
)
SELECT p.name,
       COUNT(*)                AS big_movies,
       ROUND(AVG(big.rating), 2) AS avg_rating,
       SUM(big.votes)          AS total_votes
FROM big
CROSS JOIN crew c ON c.title_id = big.title_id
JOIN people p ON p.person_id = c.person_id
WHERE c.category IN ('actor', 'actress')
GROUP BY c.person_id
HAVING big_movies >= 5
ORDER BY avg_rating DESC, big_movies DESC
LIMIT 50

title: Actors who always work together
description: Pairs of actors who appear together in the most movies with 100k+ votes (at least 4), plus what share of the less-prolific one's big movies it covers. Heavy: uses a good chunk of your budget, and if it hits the 5 s limit, raise 100000 to 300000 in the query.
sql:
WITH big AS (
  SELECT r.title_id
  FROM ratings r JOIN titles t ON t.title_id = r.title_id
  WHERE r.votes > 100000 AND +t.type = 'movie'  -- the "+" keeps SQLite from using the type index (faster)
),
actors AS (
  SELECT c.title_id, c.person_id
  FROM big CROSS JOIN crew c ON c.title_id = big.title_id
  WHERE c.category IN ('actor', 'actress')
),
totals AS (
  SELECT person_id, COUNT(*) AS films FROM actors GROUP BY person_id
),
pairs AS (
  SELECT a.person_id AS p1, b.person_id AS p2, COUNT(*) AS together
  FROM actors a JOIN actors b
    ON b.title_id = a.title_id AND b.person_id > a.person_id
  GROUP BY a.person_id, b.person_id
  HAVING together >= 4
)
SELECT n1.name AS actor_1, n2.name AS actor_2,
       pairs.together AS films_together,
       t1.films AS actor_1_films, t2.films AS actor_2_films,
       ROUND(100.0 * pairs.together / MIN(t1.films, t2.films)) AS pct_of_smaller
FROM pairs
JOIN totals t1 ON t1.person_id = pairs.p1
JOIN totals t2 ON t2.person_id = pairs.p2
JOIN people n1 ON n1.person_id = pairs.p1
JOIN people n2 ON n2.person_id = pairs.p2
ORDER BY films_together DESC, pct_of_smaller DESC
LIMIT 50

title: Directors by average rating of their big movies
description: Directors with at least 4 movies over 100k votes, ranked by average rating.
sql:
WITH big AS (
  SELECT r.title_id, r.rating
  FROM ratings r JOIN titles t ON t.title_id = r.title_id
  WHERE r.votes > 100000 AND +t.type = 'movie'  -- the "+" keeps SQLite from using the type index (faster)
)
SELECT p.name, COUNT(*) AS big_movies, ROUND(AVG(big.rating), 2) AS avg_rating
FROM big
CROSS JOIN crew c ON c.title_id = big.title_id
JOIN people p ON p.person_id = c.person_id
WHERE c.category = 'director'
GROUP BY c.person_id
HAVING big_movies >= 4
ORDER BY avg_rating DESC, big_movies DESC
LIMIT 50

title: Most-voted titles of all time
description: The titles with the most votes, any type.
sql:
SELECT t.primary_title, t.type, t.premiered AS year, r.rating, r.votes
FROM ratings r JOIN titles t ON t.title_id = r.title_id
ORDER BY r.votes DESC
LIMIT 50

title: Filmography of a person (edit the name)
description: Change the name in the WHERE clause. Names must match exactly.
sql:
SELECT t.primary_title, t.type, t.premiered AS year, c.category, r.rating, r.votes
FROM people p
JOIN crew c ON c.person_id = p.person_id
JOIN titles t ON t.title_id = c.title_id
LEFT JOIN ratings r ON r.title_id = t.title_id
WHERE p.name = 'Humphrey Bogart'
ORDER BY r.votes DESC
LIMIT 50

title: Kevin Bacon number of an actor (edit the name)
description: How many movies apart is this person from Kevin Bacon? Searches 2 steps out from each of them and meets in the middle, so it finds numbers up to 4. Only counts actors in movies with 50k+ votes. Empty result means more than 4 steps, or the name isn't in that set. Edit the name in the people lookup.
sql:
WITH RECURSIVE
edges AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT c.title_id AS t, c.person_id AS p
  FROM ratings r
  CROSS JOIN titles x ON x.title_id = r.title_id AND x.type = 'movie'
  CROSS JOIN crew c ON c.title_id = r.title_id
  WHERE r.votes > 50000 AND c.category IN ('actor', 'actress')
),
reach(side, p, n) AS (
  SELECT 'K', 'nm0000102', 0
  UNION
  SELECT 'T', person_id, 0 FROM people WHERE name = 'Marlon Brando'
  UNION
  SELECT r.side, e2.p, r.n + 1
  FROM reach r
  JOIN edges e1 ON e1.p = r.p
  JOIN edges e2 ON e2.t = e1.t
  WHERE r.n < 2
)
SELECT MIN(a.n + b.n) AS bacon_number
FROM reach a JOIN reach b ON b.p = a.p
WHERE a.side = 'K' AND b.side = 'T'

title: Kevin Bacon path: the movies linking an actor to him (edit the name)
description: Shows the actual chain: one row per hop (actor, movie, actor) from the person you name to Kevin Bacon. Same rules as the Bacon number example. No rows means more than 4 steps, or the name isn't in that set.
sql:
WITH RECURSIVE
edges AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT c.title_id AS t, c.person_id AS p
  FROM ratings r
  CROSS JOIN titles x ON x.title_id = r.title_id AND x.type = 'movie'
  CROSS JOIN crew c ON c.title_id = r.title_id
  WHERE r.votes > 50000 AND c.category IN ('actor', 'actress')
),
reach(side, p, n, q, t) AS (
  SELECT 'K', 'nm0000102', 0, NULL, NULL
  UNION
  SELECT 'T', person_id, 0, NULL, NULL FROM people WHERE name = 'Marlon Brando'
  UNION
  SELECT r.side, e2.p, r.n + 1, r.p, e1.t
  FROM reach r
  JOIN edges e1 ON e1.p = r.p
  JOIN edges e2 ON e2.t = e1.t
  WHERE r.n < 2
),
best AS (SELECT side, p, MIN(n) AS n, q, t FROM reach GROUP BY side, p),
meet AS (
  SELECT a.p FROM best a JOIN best b ON b.p = a.p
  WHERE a.side = 'K' AND b.side = 'T'
  ORDER BY a.n + b.n LIMIT 1
),
chain(side, p, n, q, t) AS (
  SELECT b.side, b.p, b.n, b.q, b.t FROM best b JOIN meet ON b.p = meet.p
  UNION ALL
  SELECT b.side, b.p, b.n, b.q, b.t FROM chain c JOIN best b ON b.side = c.side AND b.p = c.q
)
SELECT CASE c.side WHEN 'T' THEN pq.name ELSE pp.name END AS from_actor,
       ti.primary_title || ' (' || ti.premiered || ')' AS movie,
       CASE c.side WHEN 'T' THEN pp.name ELSE pq.name END AS to_actor
FROM chain c
JOIN people pp ON pp.person_id = c.p
JOIN people pq ON pq.person_id = c.q
JOIN titles ti ON ti.title_id = c.t
WHERE c.n > 0
ORDER BY CASE c.side WHEN 'T' THEN c.n ELSE 100 - c.n END

title: Hollywood's ghosts: actors credited after they died
description: Actors whose movie came out years after their death, biggest gap first. Some are CGI resurrections, some are footage shot decades earlier, some are bad data. Movies with 25k+ votes only.
sql:
SELECT p.name,
       p.died,
       ti.primary_title AS movie,
       ti.premiered,
       ti.premiered - p.died AS years_after_death,
       REPLACE(TRIM(c.characters, '[]' || char(34)), char(34) || ',' || char(34), ' / ') AS role
FROM ratings r
CROSS JOIN titles ti ON ti.title_id = r.title_id AND ti.type = 'movie'
CROSS JOIN crew c ON c.title_id = r.title_id
CROSS JOIN people p ON p.person_id = c.person_id
WHERE r.votes > 25000
  AND c.category IN ('actor', 'actress')
  AND ti.premiered > p.died
ORDER BY years_after_death DESC, r.votes DESC
LIMIT 40

title: Vanity project test: do directors get worse when they cast themselves?
description: Directors with at least 3 movies where they also act and 3 where they don't. A negative vanity_effect means their self-starring movies rate lower. Flip ASC to DESC to see who actually benefits from putting themselves on screen.
sql:
WITH big AS (
  SELECT r.title_id, r.rating
  FROM ratings r JOIN titles t ON t.title_id = r.title_id
  WHERE r.votes > 25000 AND t.type = 'movie'
),
dirs AS (
  SELECT c.person_id, big.rating,
         MAX(c.category IN ('actor', 'actress')) AS stars
  FROM big CROSS JOIN crew c ON c.title_id = big.title_id
  WHERE c.category IN ('director', 'actor', 'actress')
  GROUP BY big.title_id, c.person_id
  HAVING MAX(c.category = 'director') = 1
)
SELECT p.name,
       COUNT(*) AS films,
       SUM(stars) AS cast_themselves,
       ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN stars = 1 THEN rating END), 2) AS avg_when_starring,
       ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN stars = 0 THEN rating END), 2) AS avg_when_not,
       ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN stars = 1 THEN rating END)
           - AVG(CASE WHEN stars = 0 THEN rating END), 2) AS vanity_effect
FROM dirs JOIN people p ON p.person_id = dirs.person_id
GROUP BY dirs.person_id
HAVING SUM(stars) >= 3 AND SUM(1 - stars) >= 3
ORDER BY vanity_effect ASC
LIMIT 25

title: The remake curse: biggest drop from original to remake
description: Pairs movies with the same title released 5+ years apart, biggest rating drop first. Flip DESC to ASC to find remakes that beat the original. Unrelated movies that merely share a title show up too, so apply judgment.
sql:
WITH big AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT t.primary_title AS title, t.premiered AS year, r.rating, r.votes
  FROM ratings r JOIN titles t ON t.title_id = r.title_id
  WHERE r.votes > 25000 AND t.type = 'movie' AND t.premiered IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT o.title,
       o.year AS original_year, o.rating AS original_rating,
       n.year AS remake_year, n.rating AS remake_rating,
       ROUND(o.rating - n.rating, 1) AS rating_drop
FROM big o JOIN big n ON n.title = o.title AND n.year > o.year + 4
ORDER BY rating_drop DESC, n.votes DESC
LIMIT 30

title: Typecast Hall of Fame: same character, most movies
description: Actors who played the exact same character in the most movies with 25k+ votes, and how many years they were stuck in the role.
sql:
WITH roles AS (
  SELECT c.person_id, c.characters AS role,
         COUNT(*) AS movies,
         MIN(ti.premiered) AS first_year, MAX(ti.premiered) AS last_year,
         AVG(r.rating) AS avg_rating
  FROM ratings r
  CROSS JOIN titles ti ON ti.title_id = r.title_id AND ti.type = 'movie'
  CROSS JOIN crew c ON c.title_id = r.title_id
  WHERE r.votes > 25000
    AND c.category IN ('actor', 'actress')
    AND c.characters IS NOT NULL
    AND c.characters NOT LIKE '%Himself%' AND c.characters NOT LIKE '%Herself%'
  GROUP BY c.person_id, c.characters
  HAVING COUNT(*) >= 4
)
SELECT p.name,
       REPLACE(TRIM(roles.role, '[]' || char(34)), char(34) || ',' || char(34), ' / ') AS role,
       roles.movies,
       roles.first_year, roles.last_year,
       roles.last_year - roles.first_year AS years_in_role,
       ROUND(roles.avg_rating, 1) AS avg_rating
FROM roles JOIN people p ON p.person_id = roles.person_id
ORDER BY roles.movies DESC, years_in_role DESC
LIMIT 40
